description_full: Brava Energia S.A. engages in the exploration and production of oil and natural gas in Brazil. It is also involved in the treatment, refining, processing, and trading of oil, gas, and derivatives. The company was formerly known as 3R Petroleum Óleo e Gás S.A. and changed its name to Brava Energia S.A. in September 2024. The company was founded in 2010 and is headquartered in Rio De Janeiro, Brazil. As of August 17, 2026, Brava Energia S.A. operates as a subsidiary of Ecopetrol Investimentos do Brasil LTDA.

financial_summary: Brava Energia S.A. is a small-cap energy business with a $1.2B market cap on $2.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +84% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 7% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 29%.

The business throws off $709M in free cash flow — roughly 34 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.45× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.2× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 1.1× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Net dilution runs at 2.0% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and within its sector the business captures 1.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
